_meta.purpose: One entry per adjustable control on a ZONE (Pro mode) or on the paint: what it is called in the UI, the exact zone field, range/default, what it does in buyer words, what it combines with, and how the planner should use it to reach a wished look.
_meta.how_to_apply: Every control is set through SpbProZone.edit(zone, spec) / SpbProZone.add(spec) (js/spb-pro-zone-kit.js). `spec_key` is the key in that spec; `zone_field` is the property on the live zone object (the thing the UI slider writes). `payload_field` is what the render request carries to the engine.
_meta.atlas_flag: Atlas item flag `o` = 'own': the item BRINGS ITS OWN colours (monolithic / most patterns' palettes). `takes` = the item takes the zone colour (plain bases: gloss, satin, matte, candy, pearl, metallic ...). See scripts/ai_atlas/README.md.
_meta.ranges_note: range = what the UI slider allows; engine_range = what the setter/engine accepts when different (UI-vs-engine differences are listed in `disagreements`).
_meta.evidence_note: evidence = file:line (line numbers drift; anchor by the function / field name). Root-relative paths. api-render = paint-booth-5-api-render.js, zones = paint-booth-2-state-zones.js, kit = js/spb-pro-zone-kit.js, engine = shokker_engine_v2.py.

render_verification.R1_hue_on_takes_colour: MEASURED (test server, ARCA sheet, gloss + solid green #2e8b2e, whole-car zone): mean hue 110 deg at hue 0; +180 -> 311 (magenta); -150 -> 338 (hot pink); -150 with saturation +30 and brightness +40 -> 338 with saturation .60->.76, value .51->.68. Rule: shift = target_hue - current_hue wrapped to -180..180 (green 110 -> pink 335 = -150 or +210). A shift of +150 gives PURPLE (278), not pink.
render_verification.R2_base_colour_on_own_colour_item: MEASURED (monolithic mc_blue_camo, own blue palette, hue 232): solid #ff69b4 DOES recolour it (hue 337) but the render is one flat pink with the camo structure gone (viewed); hue shift +110 on color 'finish' reaches hue 339 and keeps the finish's own structure (hue measured; image not viewed). So the earlier 'should not recolour' note does not hold for monolithics on this build; the solid pick flattens, the hue shift preserves.
render_verification.R3_pattern_scale: VISUAL ONLY: snake_skin_3 on satin pink, scale 0.5 renders as a dense fine scale mesh (viewed); in Overlay paint mode the pattern paints its OWN brown colours and the pink base colour is NOT visible (viewed) - recolour needs Blend mode or hue shift. My autocorrelation metric gave 34 px (1.0) vs 48 px (0.5) = not a valid size metric; the 1.0 image was not viewed side by side.
render_verification.R4_spec_pattern_strength: MEASURED on the spec preview (satin, spec_snake_scales): blue-channel (clearcoat) std 21.7 with no spec pattern, 32.6 at opacity 30, 58.7 at opacity 100 (monotone). Colour preview unchanged by design (not compared).

groups.colour: Where the zone's colour comes from and how it is shifted
groups.base_material: The base finish's own texture / strength / placement
groups.pattern: The paint PATTERN layered on the zone
groups.spec_pattern: Spec patterns: change how the surface reflects (shine / metal / clearcoat texture), not the colour
groups.region: Which pixels of the car a zone owns
groups.second_base: Extra base layers blended over the first
groups.paint_global: Settings that change the look of the whole render rather than one zone

controls.ui_label: BASE COLOR (dropdown: Use finish's own color / Use source paint (spec only) / Use solid color / From special / Custom gradient)
controls.where: Pro > zone detail panel > BASE section
controls.payload_field: base_color_mode (+ base_color, gradient_stops, gradient_direction, base_color_source, base_color_explicit=true)
controls.default: finish (new zones); older saves carry an inherited 'source'
controls.applies_to: Every base finish and monolithic. It decides where the zone's paint colour comes from.
controls.effect: finish = the material keeps its own colour; source = KEEP the car's existing paint, change only shine/texture; solid = paint the zone one exact colour; special = take colours from another finish; gradient = 2-10 colour stops across the zone.
controls.interactions: A plain 'solid' pick renders the EXACT colour (Color Lab depth/flip/underglow are opt-in; never auto-send base_color_depth). 'source' is spec-only: hue/sat/brightness still adjust the SOURCE colours. MEASURED: solid colour on a monolithic that brings its own palette recolours it but FLATTENS it to one colour (camo structure lost); a hue shift keeps the structure. Picking a mode sets baseColorModeExplicit=true (an unchosen 'source' means 'finish').
controls.planner_hint: Wanted colour is exact (hex / 'red') -> pick a base that takes the zone colour and set color:'#rrggbb'. Wanted 'keep my colours, change the shine' -> color:'source' with a Foundation (f_*) finish. Wanted a fade -> gradient with 2-5 stops. On a finish that brings its own palette solid gives a flat colour: use a hue shift to keep its structure.

controls.ui_label: Solid colour picker (appears with 'Use solid color')
controls.where: Pro > zone detail > BASE > colour swatch
controls.applies_to: Items that take the zone colour (gloss, satin, matte, candy, pearl, metallic, foundation-with-colour). Weak or ignored on monolithics that bring their own palette.
controls.effect: Paints the zone exactly this colour, with the base finish's shine on top.
controls.interactions: Only used when baseColorMode == 'solid'. baseColorStrength (0-1, payload base_color_strength) fades it over the base. Hue/sat/brightness offsets then shift this colour.
controls.planner_hint: Use for any colour the buyer names exactly. For 'pink' use #ff69b4 / hot pink #ff1493 / blush #f4a6c0; always on a base that takes colour.

controls.where: Pro > zone detail > BASE > gradient editor
controls.applies_to: Items that take the zone colour; used with baseColorMode 'gradient'.
controls.effect: Colour fades across the zone along the chosen direction (the flat paint canvas, not the 3D car).
controls.interactions: Direction is in flat-canvas space (horizontal = left to right across the sheet). baseColorScale / baseColorRotation scale / rotate the gradient art.
controls.planner_hint: 'fade from X to Y' = 2 stops; 'sunset' = 3 stops. Put it on the zone that owns the big body area.

controls.where: Pro > zone detail > BASE > Hue / Saturation / Brightness rows
controls.applies_to: Everything that renders a base colour: plain bases, monolithics (engine applies HSB after the finish paint), base+pattern compositions. Does NOT touch the spec (shine).
controls.effect: Rotates every colour in the zone round the colour wheel. MEASURED: a green (110 deg) zone: +180 -> magenta (311), -150 -> hot pink (338), +150 -> purple (278).
controls.interactions: Applied AFTER the colour mode: on 'solid' it shifts the picked colour; on 'finish'/'source' it shifts the material's own / the car's existing colours. Works together with saturation and brightness. Greys (no hue) do not change: a black/white/grey finish needs a colour mode, not hue. Pattern art colours are shifted only if the pattern is painted into the zone paint (overlay mode).
controls.planner_hint: Compute shift = target_hue - current_hue, wrapped to -180..180 (hot pink ~335, magenta 310, red 0, orange 30, yellow 60, green 120, cyan 180, blue 230, purple 275). Green camo -> pink = about -150; then saturation +30 and brightness +40 for a lighter vivid pink (measured). Check the preview and nudge by 10-20.

controls.effect: Negative = greyer / washed out, positive = more vivid.
controls.interactions: Pairs with hue: after a big hue shift colours often come out muddy, add +20..40. At -100 the colour is gone.
controls.planner_hint: 'pastel / soft' = -20..-40; 'neon / vivid / punchy' = +30..+60; 'desaturate / dull / military' = -40..-70.

controls.effect: Negative = darker, positive = lighter (up to double).
controls.interactions: Brightening a saturated colour desaturates it toward white (pink = red + brightness). Applied after hue/sat.
controls.planner_hint: 'lighter / pastel pink' = +30..+80; 'darker / deep' = -20..-50. Hot pink needs hue + saturation more than brightness.

controls.ui_label: (no slider in Pro; set by modes) Colour strength
controls.effect: How strongly the chosen colour replaces the finish's own colour (legacy crossfade).
controls.interactions: Ignored in 'finish' and 'source' modes. Superseded by the Colour Depth control when the Color Lab is active.
controls.planner_hint: Leave at 1 unless the buyer wants a tint over the finish (use 0.3-0.6).

controls.where: Pro > zone detail > BASE > Color Lab (locked until a solid / special / gradient colour is set)
controls.applies_to: Zones with a colour mode other than finish/source.
controls.effect: Candy-coat look: the colour multiplies over the zone's own structure (depth), a second hue shows in the darks (flip, chameleon feel), a gold/silver ground coat glows through (underglow).
controls.interactions: OPT-IN. Its mere presence in the payload switches the engine to the Lab pipeline, which makes a picked colour darker (a red over a dark finish cannot exceed about half brightness). NEVER auto-send base_color_depth (owner rule 2026-09-03): an exact-colour request must stay on the legacy path.
controls.planner_hint: Only when the buyer asks for candy depth / chameleon / flip colours. Not for an exact colour.

controls.where: Pro > zone detail > BASE (only meaningful for 'From special' and 'Custom gradient')
controls.applies_to: Zones whose colour comes from a special or a gradient (solid colours have nothing to scale).
controls.effect: Zooms / rotates the colour art itself without touching the material texture.
controls.interactions: Independent of Base Scale (material texture) and Pattern Scale.
controls.planner_hint: Rarely needed; use to make a gradient or a special's colour art bigger / smaller.

controls.range: 0.05x-5.0x (slider 0-1000, 1.00x at the centre; non-linear: left half 0.05-1, right half 1-5)
controls.applies_to: Base finishes with a visible texture (flake, grain, weave inside the material, fractal / dust). Flat plain bases have no texture to scale.
controls.effect: Smaller = finer, busier texture (more repeats across the car); larger = bigger grains. 0.5 = twice as fine.
controls.interactions: Spec Scale follows Base Scale until 'Independent Spec' is ticked. Does not rescale the whole canvas, only the base texture inside this zone. Not the same control as pattern scale.
controls.planner_hint: 'finer flake / tighter grain / crushed to 50%' -> baseScale 0.4-0.6 on the base; 'bigger flake' -> 1.5-3. When the buyer says 'crushed' about a PATTERN, that is the pattern scale instead (zone_pattern_scale).

controls.effect: Turns the base texture's direction.
controls.interactions: Independent of pattern rotation and spec rotation.
controls.planner_hint: 'diagonal brushed' = 45; 'vertical grain' = 90.

controls.effect: Fades the complete finish result over the original paint: 0% = the car's own paint, 100% = the full finish. (Over 100% only via the kit / saved files.)
controls.interactions: Different from 'intensity' (whole-zone strength preset 10-100) and from spec strength (shine only). Lowering it lets the source paint show through (ghosted finish).
controls.planner_hint: 'subtle / hint of / ghost' -> 30-60%; 'full' -> 100.

controls.applies_to: Every base / finish with a non-neutral material (metallic, chrome, candy).
controls.effect: Weakens (or boosts) the finish's MATERIAL: metal / roughness / clearcoat move toward neutral. Colour unchanged.
controls.interactions: Separate from Base Strength (paint). Zone spec_shift adds on top.
controls.planner_hint: 'less shiny / tone down the metal' -> 50-70%; 'more metallic' -> 120-150 (kit only).

controls.where: Pro > zone detail header (preset buttons 10-100 + custom spec/paint/bright sliders)
controls.range: 0-100 (presets in steps of 10; INTENSITY_VALUES maps each to spec/paint/bright 0.1-1.0)
controls.applies_to: The whole zone (paint + spec + brightness together) unless the 'custom' split is used.
controls.effect: Overall strength of the zone's effect on the car; lower = closer to the original paint and a calmer spec.
controls.interactions: Combines multiplicatively with base strength and spec strength. patternIntensity (payload pattern_intensity) lets the pattern keep its strength while the base is lowered.
controls.planner_hint: Use for 'dial it back / more subtle' on the whole zone; use base strength when only the finish should fade.

controls.ui_label: Spec Scale (Independent Spec checkbox) / Spec Rotation
controls.applies_to: The spec (shine) texture of the base.
controls.effect: Sizes / rotates the shine texture separately from the colour texture.
controls.interactions: Locked to Base Scale until 'Independent Spec' is ticked (the 1.0 value must be sent explicitly when independent).
controls.planner_hint: Rarely needed; use when a buyer wants fine flake shimmer on a big visible pattern.

controls.ui_label: R Metal / G Rough / B Clearcoat shifts (spec channel shift)
controls.where: Pro > zone detail > SPEC > channel shifts (and spec presets)
controls.applies_to: Every zone; applied last on top of patterns, overlays and blend modes.
controls.effect: Metal + = more metallic everywhere in the zone; Rough + = duller / matter, - = glossier; Clearcoat shift moves the gloss layer (REMEMBER B=clearcoat is inverted: 16 = max gloss, higher = duller; floor is 16).
controls.interactions: Roughness floor 15 and clearcoat floor 16 are enforced by the engine. Additive to spec strength.
controls.planner_hint: Direct 'make it satin / more matte' -> rough +40..+80 and clearcoat +30..+60; 'high gloss / wet' -> rough -40, clearcoat -10 (floors apply); 'more metal' -> metal +50..+90.

controls.ui_label: (no UI slider) imported-spec sample / remap / lighting mask
controls.effect: Absolute metal / roughness / clearcoat values (override), a low/high range remap, and the spec alpha (lighting mask).
controls.interactions: No Pro slider writes them (they are payload-only / set by the spec-sample tools): UI-vs-engine gap. The helper cannot set them via edit().
controls.planner_hint: Not reachable by the helper; use spec_shift for relative changes or pick a finish whose card has the wanted shine.
evidence: grep: no setter for specMaterialOverride in paint-booth-*.js

controls.where: legacy v6 setter (setZoneCCQuality); not in the main panel
controls.effect: Lower = a worse (hazier) clearcoat.
controls.interactions: Overlaps with the B (clearcoat) channel shift.
controls.planner_hint: Use spec_shift.clearcoat instead; ccQuality is legacy.

controls.effect: Scuffs / ages the finish (chips, dulling).
controls.interactions: Applied in a later pass after the zone is composed (engine wear_zones).
controls.planner_hint: 'worn / battle-scarred / aged' -> 25-60.

controls.where: Pro > zone detail > PATTERN > swatch picker
controls.applies_to: Patterns are paint art drawn over the base colour. Needs a base (the kit adds 'gloss' if the zone has none).
controls.effect: Paints a repeating design (camo, carbon, scales, hex, flames ...) on the zone. Camo / animal-skin patterns bring their own light/dark tones that sit on the zone colour.
controls.interactions: MEASURED: in Overlay paint mode a pattern paints its own colours (snake_skin_3 = brown) and the base colour does not show; use Blend mode (keeps paint colour) or hue shift to recolour. Pattern colours follow the base colour: in 'overlay' paint mode the pattern replaces colour, in 'blend' mode it keeps the paint colour and only modulates it (so the base colour decides the camo hue). Extra patterns stack (pattern_stack, max 4 more).
controls.planner_hint: Rattlesnake = pattern 'snake_skin_3' (hourglass viper saddles); snake_skin / snake_skin_2 are other scale styles; camo = 'multicam' / 'camo'. Pink pattern: Blend mode or hue shift.

controls.range: UI 0.10x-4.0x (slider 10-400, step 5); kit clamps 0.05-5; server accepts 0.01-10
controls.applies_to: Patterns (and the monolithic's own texture when a monolithic is the zone finish).
controls.effect: Smaller number = the pattern repeats more times = a FINER weave / smaller scales / tighter camo. 0.5 = twice as fine. Owner's 'crushed to 50%' means scale 0.5. (Viewed: 0.5 gives a dense fine scale mesh.)
controls.interactions: Separate from Base Scale (base texture) and spec-pattern scale. The car is a 2048 sheet: scale 1 can read big on the car, finer is usually right for scales / weave.
controls.planner_hint: 'finer / tighter / small scales / crushed to N%' -> scale = N/100 (fine 0.5, micro 0.35 - note the UI minimum is 0.10); 'big / bold' -> 1.6-2.2.

controls.effect: Turns the pattern (stripes / weave direction).
controls.interactions: NOTE: the engine falls back to the pattern 'rotation' for the base when base_rotation is absent (engine:17799).
controls.planner_hint: 'diagonal' = 45; 'vertical' = 90.

controls.effect: How visible the pattern is: 0 invisible, 100 full. Lower = the base colour shows through the pattern.
controls.interactions: Different from Strength (patternSpecMult): opacity fades the pattern, strength scales its paint/spec effect.
controls.planner_hint: 'subtle / faint' = 30-50; 'full' = 100; a pattern that fights the base colour -> 50-70.

controls.effect: Pattern effect in paint and spec: 0 removes the effect.
controls.interactions: Pairs with Opacity. The UI help text says spec amount is independent.
controls.planner_hint: Leave at 100; use opacity for 'subtle'.

controls.ui_label: Paint mode (Overlay - full pattern / Blend - keep paint color)
controls.applies_to: All pattern layers of the zone.
controls.effect: Overlay draws the pattern's own colours over the paint; Blend keeps the paint colour and only modulates light/dark with the pattern.
controls.interactions: In blend mode the base/zone colour (and hue shift) decides the pattern's hue - the right mode for 'camo in MY colour'.
controls.planner_hint: Wanted a pattern in a specific colour: set blend mode + colour the base. Wanted the pattern's own palette: overlay.

controls.ui_label: (no visible UI) pattern hue shift / saturation
controls.effect: Would recolour the pattern art alone.
controls.interactions: UI-vs-engine gap: the engine reads them (engine:19345) and the payload sends them (api-render:616-617) but no slider in the zone panel exposes them (only the second-base pattern has hue/sat sliders). The helper cannot set them via edit().
controls.planner_hint: To recolour a pattern use the zone hue shift or blend mode + base colour instead.

controls.ui_label: Pattern offset X/Y, placement (normal / fit zone / manual), flip H/V
controls.effect: Slides, mirrors or fits the pattern inside the zone (fit = pattern stretched into the zone's area).
controls.interactions: 'fit' changes how scale reads (a pattern fitted to a small panel).
controls.planner_hint: Only for placing a motif on a specific panel; whole-car fields leave it centred.

controls.ui_label: Add pattern layer (Pattern 2..5 on this Layer/Zone: Opacity / Scale / Rotate / Blend)
controls.where: Pro > zone detail > PATTERN > + add pattern
controls.spec_key: (not in the kit: only pattern 1 via pattern:{...})
controls.range: up to 4 extra layers (MAX_PATTERN_STACK_LAYERS=4); opacity 0-100, scale 10-400%, rotation 0-359, blend normal|multiply|screen|overlay
controls.effect: A second, third ... pattern on top of the first, each with its own size, angle and blend.
controls.interactions: Each layer has its own scale/rotation/opacity independent of pattern 1.
controls.planner_hint: 'camo with a snake-scale texture': put camo as pattern 1 (hue-shifted) and the scale pattern as pattern 2 at opacity 40-60, scale 0.4-0.6, blend multiply or overlay. The kit edit() only sets pattern 1, so use a second zone (or the UI) for the extra layer.

controls.ui_label: SPEC PATTERN layers (id, Opacity, Range, Scale, Rotate, Blend, Channels M/R/C)
controls.zone_field: specPatternStack [{pattern, opacity 0-100 (default 50), range (default 40), scale, rotation, blendMode, channels 'MRC', offsetX/Y, muted, solo}]
controls.range: opacity 0-100, scale 0.1-4 (UI) / 0.05-5 (kit), rotation 0-359, channels any of M R C, blend normal|multiply|screen|overlay
controls.default: empty; a new layer takes the spec pattern's own defaults (opacity default 50)
controls.applies_to: ANY zone. Spec patterns change shine / metal / clearcoat texture only, never the paint colour (the picture looks the same in a flat preview - check spec).
controls.effect: Adds a micro-texture to HOW the surface reflects: e.g. a reptile-scale spec makes light catch on each scale; flake spec = sparkle; brushed = directional sheen.
controls.interactions: channels decide which of Metal / Rough / Clearcoat it modulates (default inferred from the pattern's own docstring). Opacity is the strength; Range is how far values swing. Spec strength / spec shift apply on top. Not visible in the flat colour preview.
controls.planner_hint: To weave a pattern 'in' without changing colour: spec_patterns:[{id:'<reptile or scale spec>',opacity:50-70,scale:0.4-0.6,channels:'MR'}] and a satin base. Stack up to 3 layers: a fine flake (scale 0.3) + the scale pattern (0.5) + a brushed grain.

controls.where: Pro > zone detail > WHICH PIXELS (target colours)
controls.applies_to: Selects the zone's pixels by their colour in the current paint.
controls.effect: The zone covers every pixel within tolerance of the picked colour(s) (e.g. 'the red areas').
controls.interactions: Combined with exclude / part / band / rect (all must match). Lower zone index wins overlaps.
controls.planner_hint: 'turn the blue parts pink' = region.colors:['#2255cc'], tolerance 35-50, then colour / hue on the zone.

controls.ui_label: Region: layers / element / exclude / part / portion / band / rect / cells
controls.where: AI zone kit (and the Pro 'draw / select' tools, layer binding)
controls.zone_field: regionMask / spatialMask / source layers (derived from the spec)
controls.range: see SCHEMA: part names come from get_car_map; band 0-1 fractions (height = roof-line to rocker, length = front to rear); rect/cells only for details under ~12% of the sheet
controls.effect: Chooses which pixels the zone owns: a named part (hood, left side), a stripe band, the numbers / sponsors / stripes the app found, a layer, or everything / the rest.
controls.interactions: remaining:true = whatever other zones did not claim (keep it last); everything+paintable = whole-car base. exclude:['numbers','sponsors'] keeps decals out. Boxes over ~12% of the sheet are refused.
controls.planner_hint: Whole-car look = everything+paintable; a stripe = band; 'only the hood' = part. Put detail zones above the body zone.

controls.ui_label: Zone order (drag / move up-down; position 1 = top)
controls.payload_field: array order of zones[] (+ priority_override for forced-top)
controls.default: new zones go to the TOP via the kit
controls.effect: Where two zones select the same pixel, the LOWER index (higher in the list) wins; the 'remaining' catch-all must be last.
controls.interactions: The zone below only gets pixels the zone above did not claim. A zone that must show on pixels another zone also selects has to sit ABOVE it. priority_override forces a zone to claim before earlier ones.
controls.planner_hint: Add detail / accent zones at 'top'; the body base last. If a new zone does not show, it is probably underneath a zone that already claimed those pixels.

controls.ui_label: Mute (eye / speaker icon on the zone)
controls.payload_field: (muted zones are dropped from the payload)
controls.effect: Temporarily removes the zone from the render (the car shows what is under it).
controls.interactions: A muted zone does not claim pixels, so zones below it take them.
controls.planner_hint: 'try without the stripes' -> mute instead of delete (reversible).

controls.ui_label: Base Overlay Layer 2 (+ 3rd / 4th / 5th): base, colour, strength, scale, pattern
controls.where: Pro > zone detail > BASE OVERLAY LAYERS
controls.range: strength 0-100; scale 0.1-5; up to 5 base layers total
controls.effect: A second material blended over the first (e.g. metallic flake over a candy).
controls.interactions: Each overlay can carry its own pattern with hue/sat/brightness and its own spec pattern stack. The base overlay's colour is separate from the zone's base colour.
controls.planner_hint: 'candy with flake on top' -> base candy + second_base flake at strength 40-70.

controls.payload_field: base_color_explicit (always true), base_color_depth (only when the Lab was touched)
controls.effect: explicit=true means the dropdown's chosen mode is authoritative (source mode keeps the car's paint); depth absent = exact-colour legacy path.
controls.interactions: Never auto-send base_color_depth: it darkens an exact colour. Every payload builder must send base_color_explicit.
controls.planner_hint: Never set baseColorDepth from the helper unless the buyer asks for candy depth.

disagreements.engine: setters and engine clamp to 0-200% (kit also 0-200)
disagreements.note: values over 100 only reachable via the kit / saved files; the slider display would clamp them.
kit can write 0.05 or 5 which the slider cannot show; a slider touch re-clamps to 0.10-4.0.

disagreements.ui: no slider in the zone panel
disagreements.note: engine feature with no zone-panel control.

disagreements.engine: falls back to rotation for the base when base_rotation absent (engine:17799)
disagreements.note: a pattern rotation can leak into the base texture rotation when base_rotation is not sent (compactDefaults omits 0).
